vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: glm-master-skill
Version: 1.0.4

The glm-master-skill is a documentation-only bundle that serves as a directory for other GLM-related skills. It contains no executable code, scripts, or subprocess calls, focusing entirely on providing installation instructions via 'npx clawhub' and links to official GitHub repositories (github.com/zai-org). The instructions in SKILL.md are transparent and aligned with the stated purpose of guiding users to relevant tools.

llm.summary: This is a documentation-only master skill that is internally consistent with its stated purpose, with a minor mismatch: the guide tells users to set an API key (ZHIPU_API_KEY) even though the skill metadata declares no required env vars.

dimensions.detail: The name/description claim a documentation-only master skill for the GLM ecosystem. The SKILL.md provides a catalog of GLM skills, install instructions, and links — all consistent with the stated purpose. No code, installs, or unexpected privileges are present in the skill bundle.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions are documentation-only and do not instruct the agent to execute local scripts. They do, however, instruct a human/user (or an agent acting as a UI) to run commands like `npx clawhub@latest install <skill-name>` and `git clone ...`, and to set the ZHIPU_API_KEY environment variable and modify shell config files (e.g., ~/.zshrc). These user-directed actions are appropriate for an installer guide but should be followed only after reviewing the target package/repo. The SKILL.md also instructs agents to open other skills' SKILL.md files for installation details, which is within scope for a master documentation skill.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec in the skill metadata (instruction-only). The doc recommends using `npx clawhub@latest` as the primary install method; that is a legitimate user-facing recommendation but carries the usual risk that `npx` will fetch and execute remote code at install time. This is expected for a guide that points users to npm-based installers, but users should verify the `clawhub` package and referenced GitHub repositories before running `npx`.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The metadata lists no required environment variables, but the SKILL.md explicitly instructs users to set `ZHIPU_API_KEY` for GLM skills. Requesting that API key is proportional to the documented downstream GLM skills, but the SKILL.md referencing an env var that the metadata does not declare is an inconsistency worth noting. No unrelated credentials or excessive variables are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent presence (always: false), does not include code that would write to system configs, and does not require changes to other skills' configurations. It merely provides documentation and links.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This master skill is documentation-only and appears to be what it says. Before following its install instructions: 1) Inspect the target skill's SKILL.md and the referenced GitHub repo before running any install commands. 2) Be cautious running `npx clawhub@latest` because npx fetches and executes remote code — verify the `clawhub` package and its publisher. 3) The guide tells you to set ZHIPU_API_KEY (and possibly add it to ~/.zshrc); only add API keys you trust, prefer least-privilege keys, and consider using a local secrets manager rather than placing keys in shell rc files. 4) If you want tighter assurance, clone repositories locally and review install scripts instead of using npx directly. The single metadata inconsistency is that the SKILL.md references ZHIPU_API_KEY while the skill metadata declares no required env vars — this is likely an oversight, not malicious, but worth noting.
